The A/B naming is explicitly positional (A=P_ad P_bc, B=P_ab P_cd uniformly), consistent with KnotTheory X[a,b,c,d] documentation; headline claims (deficit, adequacy-as-conjunction, gT) are invariant under global A/B swap, and the A-only/B-only split is well-defined under the stated convention. The extremal proof is exhaustive computational proof (certified enumeration with exact integer arithmetic and byte-level replay), not an analytic theorem; this is correctly framed as a table-maximum certificate conditional on the committed minimal diagrams and the KnotAtlas source copy, with diagram-dependence explicitly disclosed. originality.rationale: Substantive comparison (not timestamp/search): (1) KnotAtlas Jones Polynomial page tabulates Jones values (2110 values on 2226 knots/links via KB0/KB1 Kauffman-bracket code) but publishes no deficit distribution, adequacy flags, |sA|/|sB| counts, diagram Turaev genera, maximal-deficit value D* with witnesses, or deficit-1 breadth-(c-1) verification. (2) Live K11n19/K11n57 pages publish individual Jones polynomials (confirming span 4 and span 5 respectively) but no sorted deficit census, adequacy/state-circle join, or maximality proof. (3) Thistlethwaite 1988 proves the general breadth<=c bound and breadth c-1 characterization for connected prime diagrams -- no complete deficit census, adequacy join, or named maximal-deficit extremals through 11 crossings. (4) Dasbach-Futer-Kalfagianni-Lin-Stoltzfus (math/0605571, JCTB 2008) proves general Jones-from-ribbon-graph theorems and span inequalities for all diagrams -- no exact sorted deficit distribution with per-diagram certificates at this scope. (5) Armond-Lowrance (AGT 2017) classifies low-Turaev-genus diagrams in general -- no replayable 11-crossing span-deficit census with witnesses. Span alone is readable from published Jones tables by subtraction, but the joined artifact (independently recomputed spans/deficits PLUS per-diagram adequacy flags, all-A/all-B circle counts, diagram Turaev genera, proved unique D*=7 at K11n19 with full single-flip logs, and 18-member deficit-1 adequacy+gT=1 certificates) requires new per-diagram computation and is absent from all checked priors. Not a renamed implementation or database scrape: skein recursion is re-executed from PDs (801/801 exact matches pin the pipeline) and adequacy/gT are newly computed. Priority is established by substantive absence, not by timestamp or failed search.

value.rationale: Strongest headline judged separately: unique maximal Jones-span deficit D*=7 at K11n19 over all 801 prime knots through 11 crossings, with the full recomputed deficit distribution, deficit<=1-iff-adequate lockstep, and deficit-1 adequacy-plus-gT=1 certificates. Object is natural (standard Hoste-Thistlethwaite complete range through 11 crossings, the first range with rich adequate/inadequate and Turaev genus 0/1/2 populations -- a classification boundary, not an arbitrary slice). Invariant was motivated before computation by the recognized KMT-sharpness / span-vs-adequacy-vs-Turaev-genus program (Kauffman-Murasugi-Thistlethwaite, Thistlethwaite breadth bound, Dasbach-Lin, Armond-Lowrance/Kim). Value is not known or mechanically implied: it requires exact 2^c state-sum recomputation plus state-surface combinatorics and exhaustive sorting; no prior publishes D*, the distribution, or the lockstep. A future researcher testing span-vs-genus bounds, adequacy/almost-alternating classifications, or Khovanov-width-vs-span comparisons could reasonably need the precise D* witness, the 18-member deficit-1 list, and the per-diagram (sA,sB,gT) rows. Under the exact-invariant clause this rigorously established narrow datum is independently worth retrieving despite containing no new general theorem; certification strengthens but does not substitute for this substantive boundary, which is present here.

residual_risks: Reference-data risk: Jones values and PD/DT diagrams are conditioned on the KnotAtlas source copy (katlas_source.json); a source error would propagate, though 801/801 independent skein recomputation plus sign/ncomp cross-checks make silent error unlikely.

Convention risk: adequacy A-only/B-only split is stated under the uniform positional A=P_ad P_bc convention; literature using crossing-sign-dependent A/B naming could swap the A-only (73) vs B-only (145) labels, but adequate-as-conjunction, gT, deficit, and D* are unaffected.

Diagram-dependence: adequacy, |sA|, |sB|, gT are diagram invariants of the committed minimal diagrams (disclosed); only deficit d=c-span is a knot invariant. Extremal uniqueness is over this closed finite table.

Computational-proof scope: maximality is proved by exhaustive exact enumeration with replay transcripts, not by an analytic bound; correctness rests on the audited stdlib-only pipeline rather than a hand proof.
